mcq_options.text: Can be seen with the eye

items.prompt:
Matter is best defined as anything that:

A) Has mass and occupies space
B) Can be seen with the eye
C) Is always solid
D) Has a fixed shape
items.correct_answer: A) Has mass and occupies space

items.prompt:
The three common states in which matter ordinarily exists are:

A) Element, mixture and compound
B) Solid, liquid and gas
C) Atom, molecule and ion
D) Acid, base and salt

A substance with a fixed shape and a fixed volume is a:

A) Liquid
B) Gas
C) Solid
D) Plasma

A substance with a fixed volume but no fixed shape is a:

A) Solid
B) Gas
C) Crystal
D) Liquid

A substance that has neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume is a:

A) Gas
B) Solid
C) Liquid
D) Colloid

The kinetic theory of matter states that the particles of matter are:

A) Permanently at rest
B) In constant random motion
C) Always evenly heated
D) Joined by rigid rods

The change of a solid directly into a liquid on heating is called:

A) Sublimation
B) Condensation
C) Melting
D) Freezing

The change of a liquid into a gas throughout its bulk at a fixed temperature is:

A) Evaporation
B) Melting
C) Deposition
D) Boiling

The escape of liquid particles from the surface of a liquid below its boiling point is:

A) Evaporation
B) Boiling
C) Condensation
D) Sublimation

The change of a gas (vapour) into a liquid on cooling is called:

A) Evaporation
B) Condensation
C) Sublimation
D) Melting

A substance that changes directly from solid to gas without melting undergoes:

A) Boiling
B) Condensation
C) Sublimation
D) Freezing

Which of the following substances sublimes readily on heating?

A) Sodium chloride
B) Copper
C) Glass
D) Ammonium chloride

The change of a liquid into a solid on cooling is known as:

A) Freezing (solidification)
B) Melting
C) Boiling
D) Sublimation

The spreading of one substance through another due to particle motion is:

A) Filtration
B) Diffusion
C) Decantation
D) Crystallisation

As a solid is heated, the kinetic energy of its particles:

A) Increases
B) Decreases
C) Stays exactly the same
D) Becomes zero

mcq_options.text: The weight of the gas particles
Collisions of gas particles with the walls

items.prompt:
The pressure exerted by a gas on the walls of its container is caused by:

A) The weight of the gas particles
B) Collisions of gas particles with the walls
C) Attraction between particles
D) The colour of the gas
items.correct_answer: B) Collisions of gas particles with the walls

items.prompt:
In general, particles are most closely packed in the:

A) Liquid state
B) Gaseous state
C) Solid state
D) Vapour state

The state of matter consisting of ionised gas at very high temperature is:

A) Solid
B) Colloid
C) Crystal
D) Plasma

mcq_options.text: Remains constant while the change occurs

items.prompt:
During melting and boiling, the temperature of a pure substance:

A) Remains constant while the change occurs
B) Rises steadily
C) Falls steadily
D) Doubles each minute
items.correct_answer: A) Remains constant while the change occurs

items.prompt:
When a liquid is heated to a gas, the spacing between its particles:

A) Decreases
B) Increases greatly
C) Stays the same
D) Becomes zero

A substance that cannot be split into simpler substances by ordinary chemical means is a(n):

A) Compound
B) Mixture
C) Element
D) Solution

A substance formed when two or more elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio is a(n):

A) Mixture
B) Element
C) Alloy
D) Compound

A material made of two or more substances not chemically combined is a:

A) Mixture
B) Compound
C) Element
D) Molecule

The method used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid is:

A) Distillation
B) Filtration
C) Evaporation
D) Chromatography

To obtain common salt from salt solution, the most suitable method is:

A) Filtration
B) Decantation
C) Evaporation
D) Magnetisation

The method used to obtain pure water from sea water is:

A) Filtration
B) Decantation
C) Sublimation
D) Simple distillation

A mixture of two miscible liquids with different boiling points is best separated by:

A) Fractional distillation
B) Filtration
C) Crystallisation
D) Sublimation

Crude petroleum is separated into its useful fractions industrially by:

A) Filtration
B) Fractional distillation
C) Sublimation
D) Chromatography

The method used to separate the coloured components of a dye is:

A) Filtration
B) Distillation
C) Chromatography
D) Decantation

A mixture of ammonium chloride and salt is best separated by:

A) Filtration
B) Distillation
C) Magnetisation
D) Sublimation

A mixture of iron filings and sulphur powder can be separated using a:

A) Magnet
B) Filter paper
C) Distillation flask
D) Separating funnel

Two immiscible liquids such as oil and water are best separated using a:

A) Filter funnel
B) Separating funnel
C) Burette
D) Pipette

Carefully pouring off a clear liquid from a settled solid is called:

A) Filtration
B) Distillation
C) Decantation
D) Evaporation

The method used to obtain pure crystals of a soluble salt such as copper(II) sulphate is:

A) Sublimation
B) Filtration
C) Decantation
D) Crystallisation

In filtration, the solid left on the filter paper is called the:

A) Residue
B) Filtrate
C) Distillate
D) Solute

In filtration, the clear liquid that passes through the filter paper is the:

A) Residue
B) Filtrate
C) Sediment
D) Distillate

mcq_options.text: Has a fixed and sharp melting/boiling point

items.prompt:
A pure substance is best identified by the fact that it:

A) Is always white
B) Cannot dissolve in water
C) Has a fixed and sharp melting/boiling point
D) Is always a metal
items.correct_answer: C) Has a fixed and sharp melting/boiling point

items.prompt:
The presence of an impurity in a solid usually causes its melting point to:

A) Rise sharply
B) Stay exactly the same
C) Become exactly 100 °C
D) Lower and become less sharp
items.correct_answer: D) Lower and become less sharp

mcq_options.text: Its components keep their own properties
It always has a fixed composition
It can only be separated chemically
It is always a single colour

items.prompt:
Which statement about a mixture is correct?

A) Its components keep their own properties
B) It always has a fixed composition
C) It can only be separated chemically
D) It is always a single colour
items.correct_answer: A) Its components keep their own properties

items.prompt:
Brass, an example of an alloy, is best described as a:

A) Pure element
B) Mixture of copper and zinc
C) Compound of iron and carbon
D) Solution of salt in water
items.correct_answer: B) Mixture of copper and zinc

items.prompt:
Air is correctly classified as a:

A) Pure compound
B) Single element
C) Mixture of gases
D) Chemically combined substance

Using a solvent to dissolve and remove one component of a mixture is called:

A) Filtration
B) Sublimation
C) Decantation
D) Solvent extraction

Spinning a suspension at high speed to separate a fine solid from a liquid is:

A) Centrifuging
B) Filtration
C) Distillation
D) Evaporation

The sub-atomic particle that carries a positive charge is the:

A) Electron
B) Neutron
C) Proton
D) Photon

The sub-atomic particle that carries a negative charge is the:

A) Proton
B) Neutron
C) Nucleus
D) Electron

The sub-atomic particle that carries no charge is the:

A) Neutron
B) Proton
C) Electron
D) Ion

The protons and neutrons of an atom are found in the:

A) Electron shells
B) Nucleus
C) Valence shell
D) Outer orbit

The atomic number of an element is the number of:

A) Neutrons in the nucleus
B) Electrons plus neutrons
C) Protons in the nucleus
D) Protons plus neutrons

The mass number of an atom is the total number of:

A) Protons and electrons
B) Electrons and neutrons
C) Protons only
D) Protons and neutrons

An atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. The number of neutrons it contains is:

A) 12
B) 11
C) 23
D) 34

In a neutral atom of atomic number 17, the number of electrons is:

A) 18
B) 17
C) 35
D) 0

Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers are called:

A) Isomers
B) Allotropes
C) Isotopes
D) Ions

Two isotopes of an element differ in the number of:

A) Protons
B) Electrons
C) Valence electrons
D) Neutrons

Chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 have the same number of protons but different numbers of:

A) Neutrons
B) Electrons
C) Protons
D) Shells

Chlorine consists of 75% Cl-35 and 25% Cl-37. Its relative atomic mass is:

A) 36.0
B) 35.5
C) 37.0
D) 35.0

The arrangement of electrons in the shells of an atom is called its:

A) Atomic number
B) Valency
C) Electron configuration
D) Mass number

The maximum number of electrons that the first (K) shell of an atom can hold is:

A) 8
B) 18
C) 1
D) 2

The maximum number of electrons that the second (L) shell can hold is:

A) 8
B) 2
C) 18
D) 32

The electron configuration of a sodium atom (atomic number 11) is:

A) 2, 8, 8
B) 2, 8, 1
C) 8, 2, 1
D) 2, 9

The electron configuration of a chlorine atom (atomic number 17) is:

A) 2, 7, 8
B) 2, 8, 8
C) 2, 8, 7
D) 7, 8, 2

An atom with the configuration 2, 8, 2 has how many valence electrons?

A) 8
B) 12
C) 10
D) 2

Atoms tend to react in order to achieve a stable outer shell containing:

A) Eight electrons (an octet)
B) Two electrons only
C) Eighteen electrons
D) Zero electrons

An atom that loses one electron becomes:

A) A negatively charged ion
B) A positively charged ion
C) A neutron
D) A molecule

An atom that gains two electrons becomes an ion with a charge of:

A) 2+
B) 1-
C) 2-
D) 0

The scientist whose atomic theory proposed that elements are made of tiny indivisible atoms was:

A) Isaac Newton
B) Michael Faraday
C) Antoine Lavoisier
D) John Dalton

The experiment that showed the atom has a small dense positively charged nucleus was performed by:

A) Rutherford
B) Mendeleev
C) Boyle
D) Avogadro

A horizontal row of elements in the periodic table is called a:

A) Group
B) Period
C) Family
D) Block

A vertical column of elements in the periodic table is called a:

A) Period
B) Series
C) Group
D) Row

Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of:

A) Neutrons
B) Protons
C) Shells
D) Valence electrons

Elements in the same period of the periodic table have the same number of:

A) Electron shells
B) Valence electrons
C) Neutrons
D) Protons

The Group 1 elements (Li, Na, K) are collectively known as the:

A) Halogens
B) Alkali metals
C) Noble gases
D) Alkaline earth metals

The Group 7 elements (F, Cl, Br, I) are collectively called the:

A) Alkali metals
B) Noble gases
C) Halogens
D) Transition metals

The Group 0 (Group 8) elements such as helium and neon are called the:

A) Halogens
B) Alkali metals
C) Metalloids
D) Noble (inert) gases

The noble gases are generally unreactive because their outer shells are:

A) Completely filled
B) Half filled
C) Empty
D) Single electron

The scientist who arranged elements in order of atomic mass and predicted undiscovered elements was:

A) Dalton
B) Mendeleev
C) Rutherford
D) Moseley

The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing:

A) Atomic mass
B) Density
C) Atomic number
D) Melting point

Metals are generally found on which side of the periodic table?

A) Far right
B) Top right corner only
C) Bottom row only
D) Left and centre

Across a period from left to right, the atomic radius generally:

A) Decreases
B) Increases
C) Stays constant
D) Doubles

Down a group of the periodic table, the atomic radius generally:

A) Decreases
B) Increases
C) Stays constant
D) Falls to zero

Across a period from left to right, metallic character generally:

A) Increases
B) Stays the same
C) Decreases
D) Is unchanged

Across a period from left to right, the first ionisation energy generally:

A) Decreases
B) Stays constant
C) Becomes zero
D) Increases

Down Group 1 (alkali metals), reactivity with water generally:

A) Increases
B) Decreases
C) Stays constant
D) Stops completely

Down Group 7 (halogens), reactivity generally:

A) Increases
B) Decreases
C) Stays constant
D) Doubles each element

Elements in Group 2 of the periodic table have a combining power (valency) of:

A) 1
B) 3
C) 2
D) 0

The block of metals between Groups 2 and 3 that often form coloured compounds are the:

A) Alkali metals
B) Halogens
C) Noble gases
D) Transition metals

An element such as silicon that shows properties of both metals and non-metals is a:

A) Metalloid
B) Halogen
C) Noble gas
D) Alkali metal

The period number of an element tells us its number of:

A) Valence electrons
B) Occupied electron shells
C) Neutrons
D) Protons only

For a main-group element, the group number is equal to its number of:

A) Shells
B) Neutrons
C) Valence electrons
D) Protons

A chemical bond formed by the complete transfer of electrons from one atom to another is:

A) Covalent bond
B) Metallic bond
C) Hydrogen bond
D) Ionic (electrovalent) bond

A chemical bond formed by the sharing of electrons between atoms is a:

A) Covalent bond
B) Ionic bond
C) Metallic bond
D) Dative bond only

The bonding that involves a lattice of positive ions in a sea of mobile electrons is:

A) Ionic bonding
B) Metallic bonding
C) Covalent bonding
D) Hydrogen bonding

A covalent bond in which both shared electrons come from the same atom is a:

A) Ionic bond
B) Metallic bond
C) Coordinate (dative) bond
D) Pure covalent bond

Sodium chloride is held together by which type of bond?

A) Covalent bond
B) Metallic bond
C) Hydrogen bond
D) Ionic bond

The bonds within a molecule of water (H2O) are:

A) Covalent bonds
B) Ionic bonds
C) Metallic bonds
D) Dative bonds

mcq_options.text: Have high melting points and conduct when molten

items.prompt:
Ionic compounds generally:

A) Are gases at room temperature
B) Have high melting points and conduct when molten
C) Never dissolve in water
D) Conduct electricity as solids
items.correct_answer: B) Have high melting points and conduct when molten

mcq_options.text: Have low melting points and do not conduct electricity

items.prompt:
Simple molecular (covalent) substances generally:

A) Have very high melting points
B) Always conduct electricity
C) Have low melting points and do not conduct electricity
D) Are all ionic in water
items.correct_answer: C) Have low melting points and do not conduct electricity

items.prompt:
An ionic compound conducts electricity only when:

A) In the solid state
B) Completely dry
C) Frozen solid
D) Molten or dissolved in water
items.correct_answer: D) Molten or dissolved in water
